about: The site's official, production-ready Bible questions. Built by scripts/build-question-bank.py from Research/BibleQuizCorpus/normalized/; answers are as the sources printed them and are not yet fact-checked.
tagging: books, testament and topic are set by fixed word lists and the references (scripts/question_tags.py), not checked by hand; a question may sit under a near topic. passages, people, places and subjects are set by Claude Haiku (scripts/question_model_tags.py); every passage exists in the BSB, and its check says whether the answer's words are in it ("matched") or not ("exists").

questions.question: According to Psalm 119:105, God's word is a what to my feet?
questions.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0, granted by the site's own Terms of Service
questions.attribution: Required by CC BY-SA 4.0: credit Ministry-To-Children.com (Tony Kummer) and license any adaptation under the same or a compatible licence.

audit.why: The original asked about book sales, which the Bible does not address, and had no reference or real wrong choices, so it now asks what Psalm 119:105 says about God's word: "a lamp to my feet".

grounding.note: Psalm 119:105 says "Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path," so the answer "A lamp" is stated directly.

questions.question: What four books tell about Jesus' life on earth?
questions.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0, granted by the site's own Terms of Service
questions.attribution: Required by CC BY-SA 4.0: credit Ministry-To-Children.com (Tony Kummer) and license any adaptation under the same or a compatible licence.

audit.why: The answer is right (the four Gospels), but the question had no Bible reference, so one was added and the possessive "Jesus'" was tidied.

grounding.note: No shown verse names these four books. Luke 1:1-4 mentions "many" earlier accounts and John 20:30-31 mentions unwritten signs, but neither lists Matthew, Mark, Luke, or John. The answer comes from how the New Testament is arranged.

questions.question: In John 8, when the scribes and Pharisees brought a woman caught in adultery, where did Jesus write with His finger?

questions.attribution: Required by CC BY-SA 4.0: credit Ministry-To-Children.com (Tony Kummer) and license any adaptation under the same or a compatible licence.

audit.why: The Bible never says which books Jesus did or did not write, so the question was reworded to ask about the one time it records Jesus writing: on the ground with His finger (John 8:6).

grounding.note: John 8:6 says Jesus bent down and began to write on the ground with His finger, and John 8:8 repeats that He wrote on the ground.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 31:9, who wrote down the law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi?
questions.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0, granted by the site's own Terms of Service
questions.attribution: Required by CC BY-SA 4.0: credit Ministry-To-Children.com (Tony Kummer) and license any adaptation under the same or a compatible licence.

audit.why: The Bible gives no word counts for its writers, and one wrong choice repeated the right answer's number, so the question now asks what Deuteronomy 31:9 says: Moses wrote down the law.

grounding.note: Deuteronomy 31:9 says that Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark, and to the elders of Israel.

questions.question: Which Gospel opens with the words, "This is the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God"?
questions.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0, granted by the site's own Terms of Service

audit.why: The Bible does not say which Gospel was written first, so the question now asks which Gospel opens with the words of Mark 1:1, and a reference was added.

grounding.note: Mark 1:1 gives the opening words, but the verse does not name the book; "Mark" is the traditional title of the Gospel that begins at that verse.

questions.question: Which Gospel ends by saying that if every one of the other things Jesus did were written down, the whole world would not have room for the books?
questions.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0, granted by the site's own Terms of Service
questions.attribution: Required by CC BY-SA 4.0: credit Ministry-To-Children.com (Tony Kummer) and license any adaptation under the same or a compatible licence.

audit.why: The original question asked about the order the Gospels were written, which the Bible doesn't say. It now asks about the ending of John (John 21:25), and the answer is still John.

grounding.note: John 21:25 is the closing verse of the Gospel of John and says that if all Jesus did were written down, the world could not hold the books. The book named is John.

options: Their enduring hope in our Lord Jesus Christ
Their joyful giving to the poor
Their steady prayer for the church
questions.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0, granted by the site's own Terms of Service
questions.attribution: Required by CC BY-SA 4.0: credit Ministry-To-Children.com (Tony Kummer) and license any adaptation under the same or a compatible licence.
questions.answer_choice: Their enduring hope in our Lord Jesus Christ

audit.why: The Bible doesn't say which letter Paul wrote first, and Galatians is also a likely candidate, so the question now asks what Paul says in 1 Thessalonians 1:3.

grounding.note: 1 Thessalonians 1:3 says Paul recalls before God "your enduring hope in our Lord Jesus Christ," alongside their work of faith and labor of love.

questions.question: What did the people at Babel say they would build?
questions.answer: A city with a tower that reaches to the heavens.
options: A temple with an altar to the LORD
A wall to keep out their enemies
A city with a tower that reaches to the heavens.
A great ship to escape another flood
questions.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0, granted by the site's own Terms of Service
questions.attribution: Required by CC BY-SA 4.0: credit Ministry-To-Children.com (Tony Kummer) and license any adaptation under the same or a compatible licence.
questions.answer_choice: A city with a tower that reaches to the heavens.

audit.why: The "stars" and "city" choices were also close to true, the answer's wording did not match the question or the BSB ("a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens"), and there was no reference, so I reworded it and replaced the wrong choices.

grounding.note: Genesis 11:4 states that the people said, "let us build for ourselves a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens," which matches the printed answer.

questions.question: At the tower of Babel, what did the LORD do that led the people to be scattered over the whole earth?
questions.answer: He confused their language so they could not understand one another.
options: He struck the tower with fire from heaven
He confused their language so they could not understand one another.
He sent a second flood over the land
questions.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0, granted by the site's own Terms of Service
questions.attribution: Required by CC BY-SA 4.0: credit Ministry-To-Children.com (Tony Kummer) and license any adaptation under the same or a compatible licence.
questions.answer_choice: He confused their language so they could not understand one another.

audit.why: The question had no reference and no setting, and one wrong choice ("sent them away separately") was too close to the Bible's "scattered them", so I added Genesis 11:1-9, named Babel, and replaced two wrong choices.

grounding.note: Genesis 11:7 says the LORD would confuse their language so they could not understand one another's speech, and Genesis 11:9 says He confused the language of the whole world.

questions.question: What do we mean when we say God is a trinity?
questions.answer: God expresses Himself in three Persons—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. While each Person of the Trinity has distinct qualities, all three Persons of the Trinity are made of the same stuff. Each Person is fully God, not one-third God. You cannot divide the Trinity; there is only one God.

One God revealed in three different modes or forms at different times

questions.question: What does the Bible tell us about Jesus?
questions.answer: Christ is the eternal Son of God. Joseph took care of Jesus like a dad, but God is His real Father. Conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary, He had a real body and a human spirit. Jesus is fully God and fully human.
options: A created being, the greatest of God's creatures, but not God Himself
Born of Mary by Joseph; adopted by God as His Son at baptism
Eternal Son of God, conceived by Holy Spirit, born of Mary, fully God and human
God's Son in spirit; He only appeared to have a real human body

questions.answer: To die on the cross as a substitute for our sins. By taking our punishment, He secured the forgiveness of our sins.

Die on the cross as a substitute for our sins, securing forgiveness
To demonstrate God's love but not to actually pay for our sins

Jesus stayed on earth in His disciples and remains invisible

He will return invisibly but will not judge anyone
He has already returned in the form of the Holy Spirit

questions.question: Who is the Holy Spirit?
questions.answer: The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of God and is fully divine.

The Holy Spirit is a created being sent by God to help us
The Holy Spirit is less divine than God the Father and Son
The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of God and is fully divine.

questions.question: What are some things the Holy Spirit did in the Bible days?
questions.answer: He was involved in the creation of the world. He inspired men to write the Scriptures. He empowered Jesus in His earthly ministry. He raised Jesus from the dead.

He was sent only after Pentecost, took no part in creation, and never spoke through prophets

He was involved in creation, inspired men to write Scripture, empowered Jesus, and raised Him

questions.question: What does the Bible teach about humankind?
questions.answer: Mankind is the special creation of God, made in God's own image as His highest creation. He created them male and female; each person was born a boy or a girl as a part of God's good plan. Our life purpose is to know God and enjoy Him forever.
options: Evolved from animals and differ only in degree, not essential nature
Made in God's image but destined to achieve God-like power
In God's image, male and female, with purpose to know and enjoy God
Created as servants of God with no significance or special value

questions.question: Did God create people bad or good?
questions.answer: In the beginning man was innocent of sin. God created man with freedom of choice. By his free choice man sinned against God and brought sin and death into the human race.
options: God created man both innocent and with a natural inclination to sin
God created man innocent but without any freedom of choice, so he could not refuse sin
Created innocent with free choice, man sinned, bringing sin and death
God predestined man to sin so that Christ could provide salvation

questions.question: Why is there so much sin in the world today?
questions.answer: After the temptation of Satan, man fell from his original innocence. options: Satan caused all humans to sin immediately upon their birth
Man fell through Satan's temptation, so all are born inclined to sin
People sin because they live in a sinful environment, not by nature
Satan's temptation affected only Adam and Eve, not all people

questions.question: What is sin?
questions.answer: Sin is anything a person thinks, says, or does that is contrary to how God tells us to live. Anything that is not done as an act of faith or for the glory of God is sin. Every sin deserves God's punishment.
options: Thoughts and feelings are not sinful; only deliberate actions are
Sin is only when we intentionally break rules we know about
Contrary to God's will or not done as faith for God's glory
Only actions that harm others or break human laws constitute sin

questions.question: Even though everyone offends God by their sins, does He still consider people to be of value?
questions.answer: Every human being is greatly valued by God and every human life is sacred. We know this because God created man in His own image and because Christ died for people. Therefore, every person of every race should be respected and treated with Christian love.
options: Only redeemed people are truly valued by God; unbelievers have lesser worth
God values people according to their good works and moral accomplishments in life
Human life becomes sacred only after baptism and personal profession of Christian faith
Every human being is greatly valued by God; God created us in His image and Christ died for us

questions.answer: Because God is holy He hates sin. Because He is a God of justice He must punish those responsible for sin. Sin separates us from God and brings us under condemnation.

God tolerates sin if we confess it and promise to improve
Sin harms us but God overlooks it because of His mercy
God's punishment for sin is harsh, but His love prevents Him from enforcing it

questions.question: How does the Bible teach that a person is saved?
questions.answer: Only the grace of God can bring man into fellowship with God. Salvation is possible because Jesus died on the cross and shed His own blood to obtain forgiveness of sins. Salvation is offered freely to all who accept Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior. There is no salvation apart from personal faith in Jesus Christ.
options: Salvation is through baptism and faith in Jesus Christ as Lord
Salvation comes through faith in Christ combined with good works and obedience
Salvation requires faith in Christ plus keeping God's commandments perfectly
Salvation is only through the grace of God and personal faith in Jesus Christ

questions.question: What is election?
questions.answer: Election is God's eternal plan, formed before time began, to save sinners. Election is consistent with the sovereignty of God and with the freedom of man. Election includes evangelism; God chose to save people through spreading the Gospel. We cannot boast of our salvation. God chose us; we didn't choose Him.
options: God's foreknowledge of who would freely choose to believe in Jesus Christ
God's plan to save those who persevere in faith and obedience to His law
God's calling of believers to grow in grace and spiritual maturity after conversion
God's eternal plan, formed before time began, to save sinners through spreading the Gospel

questions.question: Do people simply make up their minds to become Christians?
questions.answer: For a person to come to Christ, God must first work in his or her heart to attract that person to Himself. This is because people are sinful and do not want God to rule their lives. God must first melt their hard hearts.
options: People must first repent of their sins before God begins to work in them
Sincere people who truly desire God are naturally and gradually drawn to Him
God must first work in their hearts to attract them, because people are sinful and unwilling for God's rule
God makes salvation possible, but people must make the final decision to accept

questions.question: How does the Holy Spirit work in lost people to bring them to Christ?

He shows the law, brings conviction, and works only through the preaching of the word
He works exclusively through Christian witness and example, not directly in the human heart
He saves people apart from the gospel, removes their need to repent, and works only in the religious

In confession of sins to a priest and sincere regret
In baptism and joining a local Christian church
In a public declaration of faith before witnesses

questions.question: What is repentance?
questions.answer: Repentance is a sincere change of mind and of attitude in which the sinner turns to God from sin.

Repentance is turning from sin and performing good works to make proper restitution

Repentance is admitting guilt before God and asking His forgiveness and restoration

grounding.note: Acts 3:19 calls sinners to repent and turn back so their sins are wiped away, and Isaiah 55:7 bids the wicked forsake their way and thoughts and return to the LORD. Together they teach turning from sin to God.

questions.question: What is saving faith?
questions.answer: Faith is trusting Jesus to do things for you that you cannot do for yourself. Faith is trusting Jesus to forgive you, to change your life, and to provide you a home in Heaven. Faith is not just believing with one's mind certain facts about God. Nor is it merely knowing the answers to questions, like those in this booklet. Faith is trusting Christ alone.
options: Believing the right facts about Jesus and understanding the gospel message correctly
Trusting Jesus to forgive you, change your life, and provide you a home in Heaven
Having faith that God exists and trusting he will help you in trouble
Knowing about Jesus and committing to follow his teachings and obey his laws

questions.question: What is regeneration?
questions.answer: The word "regeneration" means new life. It's another way of saying, "born again." The Holy Spirit makes people alive to God and renews their will, fixing their "want to." This changes the direction of a person's life.
options: Sanctification; the lifelong work of the Spirit empowering believers to overcome sinful nature
Baptism; being initiated into the church and publicly committing to Christian community
New life; being born again; the Holy Spirit makes people alive to God and changes their direction
Conversion; making a mental agreement with Christian truth and a commitment to Christ

grounding.note: Titus 3:5 calls it "new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit," and 2 Corinthians 5:17 says the one in Christ is a new creation. Ezekiel 36:26-27 supplies the new heart and Spirit that renew the will.

questions.question: What is justification?
questions.answer: To be pardoned of sin and declared right with God. Sinners are justified on the basis that Christ paid their penalty on the cross. Only those who trust Christ for salvation are justified.

questions.question: What is adoption?
questions.answer: When a person becomes a Christian, God makes him or her part of His eternal family. While everyone is God's offspring in the general way of being His creation, only Christians are children of God in this special way.
options: When a person becomes a Christian, God makes them part of His eternal family as children of God
God treats every person as His child in exactly the same way, whether or not they believe
Adoption happens only after years of faithful service and demonstration of spiritual maturity
Only church members who keep covenant with God are adopted into His eternal family

questions.question: What is sanctification?
questions.answer: When a person is born again, he or she is set apart from all else for God. Sanctification is the process of growing toward spiritual maturity through the power of the Holy Spirit living within.
options: Being set apart for God and growing toward spiritual maturity through the Holy Spirit
Becoming free from all sin and living a perfect life that pleases God
A process of removing evil desires and becoming completely holy through discipline
Growing in faith and knowledge by studying the Bible and obeying all laws

questions.question: What is the indwelling of the Holy Spirit?
questions.answer: At the very moment of salvation the Holy Spirit baptizes believers into the Body of Christ, coming to live inside them from that moment forward.
options: The Holy Spirit gives believers special abilities and spiritual gifts for God's service
After water baptism the Holy Spirit comes to dwell within the believer permanently
At salvation the Holy Spirit baptizes believers into Christ's Body and comes to live inside them
The Holy Spirit fills believers at Pentecost to empower them for witnessing

grounding.note: Romans 8:9 says the Spirit of God lives in believers, and 1 Corinthians 12:13 says all believers were baptized into one body in one Spirit. The exact timing "at the very moment" is an inference from these past-tense statements.

questions.question: What does the Holy Spirit do in the life of believers after they become Christians?
questions.answer: The Holy Spirit assures the Christian that he or she is saved. He empowers Christians in developing good character. He helps them to pray and enables them to reach the lost. He gives believers spiritual gifts by which they serve God through His church. He makes them understand the Bible and God's leadership for their lives. The Holy Spirit comforts Christians in sorrow.
options: He sanctifies completely, removes all temptation, makes believers perfect, and grants eternal rest
He assures salvation, empowers character development, helps in prayer, gives spiritual gifts, enables witness, opens Scripture, and comforts
He removes the need for prayer, replaces the church, makes Bible study unnecessary, and gives gifts only to pastors
He saves believers again each day, takes away all sorrow, keeps them from ever doubting, and gives them earthly riches

questions.question: What is glorification?
questions.answer: Glorification is when God completes salvation: believers are made like Christ, receive resurrected/glorified bodies, and share in Christ's glory as co-heirs with Him forever.
options: Exaltation; believers receiving rewards and honor in heaven for faithful Christian service
God completing salvation: being made like Christ, receiving a glorified body, and sharing in Christ's glory as co-heirs
Justification; God declaring sinners righteous in His sight through faith in Christ
Sanctification; the gradual process of God making believers increasingly more like Jesus

grounding.note: Scripture teaches glorification: believers will be like Christ and see Him as He is (1 John 3:2), share His glory as co-heirs (Romans 8:17), and have bodies transformed to be like His glorious body (Philippians 3:21).

questions.question: What is the final perseverance of the saints?
questions.answer: It means real Christians stick with it. Those who have truly been born again will never become lost again, but shall continue in faith to the end. Believers may stumble into sin for a time, making themselves miserable and grieving the Spirit; yet they shall be kept by the power of God for final salvation. Note: Some refer to this belief as "Once saved, always saved." Unfortunately this term has given some the impression that people can "get saved," live without any sign of God being at work in their lives, and then expect to go to Heaven. The proper term is "perseverance," or "the final perseverance of the saints."
options: Real Christians will continue in faith to the end and be kept by God's power for salvation
Once a person is saved, they are guaranteed to go to heaven regardless of behavior
Christians who stumble into sin can lose their salvation and be lost forever
Real Christians must obey God's commands to remain saved until the very end

questions.question: What is a local New Testament church?
questions.answer: A New Testament church is a local congregation of baptized believers, who have voluntarily joined themselves together in covenant with Christ and with each other.
options: A local congregation of baptized believers voluntarily joined together in covenant with Christ and each other
Any group of believers meeting in Jesus' name for corporate worship and prayer
The invisible universal fellowship of all believers in Christ throughout all history
A denomination of congregations under pastoral authority exercising biblical church discipline

questions.question: What are the purposes of the local church?
questions.answer: The church is to glorify God in worship and observe the ordinances of baptism and the Lord's supper. The mission of the church is to spread the gospel of Jesus Christ to the entire world through evangelism and missions. The fellowship of the church is like a "colony of heaven," providing encouragement and accountability to its members.
options: To earn salvation for its members through rituals, good works, and giving
To offer sacrifices for sin, appoint priests, and mediate between God and people
To gain political influence, enforce civil laws, and govern the surrounding community
To glorify God, observe ordinances, spread the gospel, and provide fellowship and accountability

questions.question: How is a New Testament church governed?
questions.answer: Each congregation operates under the Lordship of Christ through democratic processes. In the decision-making process, this means every member should seek to follow the leading of Jesus Christ as the Head of the church.
options: Through Presbyterian councils representing all members and making major corporate decisions
Under apostolic succession and the authority of a bishop governing multiple congregations
Under the authority of a pastor empowered to lead and direct the congregation
Each congregation operates under Christ's Lordship through democratic processes with Christ as the Head

questions.question: Who are the Biblical officers of the church?
questions.answer: Its scriptural officers are pastors and deacons. Both men and women are gifted for service, but the office of pastor is limited to biblically qualified men.
options: Pastors, deacons, elders, and bishops appointed by higher authorities
Pastors and deacons; pastor office limited to biblically qualified men
Elders and presbyters selected for life based on age
Pastors and ordained clergy chosen from the most educated members

questions.question: What is the Church Universal?
questions.answer: The New Testament speaks also of the church as the Body of Christ which includes all of the redeemed of all the ages, believers from every tribe, and tongue, and people, and nation.
options: All churches that share the same theological and denominational beliefs
The leadership of all Christian denominations working together
The Body of Christ including all redeemed of all ages and nations
The Christian churches in a particular city or region

questions.answer: Believer's baptism. Christian baptism is the immersion of a believer beneath water and raising him or her back up -- in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

Infant baptism: sprinkling or pouring water on people to cleanse from sin
Sprinkling water on believers in the name of the Father and the Son
Pouring water on baptized believers in the name of the Trinity together

Yes, but only after a period of spiritual growth and maturity demonstrated

questions.question: Is baptism required to become a Christian?
questions.answer: Baptism is a testimony that a person has already been saved. It is an outward act representing the inward baptism of the Holy Spirit that really does bring us into the family of God.

Baptism testifies that a person is already saved; it represents the Spirit's inward baptism bringing us into God's family
Baptism is only an outward symbol and has no spiritual significance or meaning
Baptism is required for salvation and brings the believer into union with Christ

questions.question: What does baptism represent?
questions.answer: Baptism pictures what Christ has done for us and in us. It symbolizes Jesus' death and resurrection, testifying, in effect, "It counts for me." It is also a testimony that the believer has died to the old life and has been raised to new life in Christ.

Jesus' death and resurrection; believer's death to old life and raising to new life in Christ
The water itself washing away sins and giving saving grace to the person baptized
The believer's commitment to Christ and promise to live faithfully and obediently

The Lord's Supper: a symbolic act of eating the bread and drinking the cup, remembering Christ's death
Fasting: abstaining from food to commemorate Christ's passion and show true devotion

questions.question: What is the Lord's Day?
questions.answer: Sunday is the first day of the week and is the Lord's Day -- that is, a day for the Lord. It celebrates the resurrection, since Jesus' resurrection took place on the first day of the week. This day should be respected as a day to spend time with God, in Christian fellowship, and in worship. Since it is a day for the Lord, a Christian should carefully consider the activities the Lord would want him or her to be involved in on this day.
options: Saturday, the Sabbath day ordained by God and never abolished for believers
Any day chosen personally as one's own day of private worship and rest
Every day equally, since God's work and rest are now purely spiritual
Sunday, first day celebrating Christ's resurrection; a day for God, fellowship, worship, and pleasing activities

grounding.note: Matthew 28:1 and Acts 20:7 put the first day of the week at the resurrection and the church's gathering; Revelation 1:10 calls that day the Lord's day, so the answer follows from these verses together.

questions.question: What is the kingdom of God?
questions.answer: In general, God rules over everything in the universe through all of history -- He is the King. The Kingdom means that God rules in a special way in the hearts of His people now. The Kingdom of God will be completed in its fullness when Jesus returns.
options: The church as God's organization extending His rule through society and nations
God's rule over all things; God ruling in believers' hearts now; to be completed when Jesus returns
God's future reign when Christ returns and establishes His visible earthly kingdom
The spiritual power of God in believers' hearts; a present internal reality only

questions.question: How will the world end?
questions.answer: According to His promise, Jesus Christ will return personally and visibly to the earth. He will return in glory; everyone will recognize Him and know He is God and in charge. The dead will be raised; and Christ will judge all people in righteousness.
options: Jesus will come again invisibly to remove believers before the final judgment
Jesus will return spiritually to believers' hearts and usher in new creation
Jesus will not return bodily, as the church gradually brings in His kingdom
Jesus will return personally and visibly in glory, raise the dead, and judge all people

grounding.note: Acts 1:11 gives Jesus' personal return in the same way He left; Matthew 24:30 adds coming in power and great glory, seen by all; Acts 17:31 gives judgment with justice; 1 Thessalonians 4:16 has the dead in Christ rising.

questions.answer: The unrighteous will be consigned to Hell, the place of everlasting punishment.

They will face God's judgment but some may receive His mercy and forgiveness

questions.answer: The righteous will appear with Christ in glory, raised with glorified bodies. They will receive their reward and dwell forever with the Lord.

The righteous will have glorified bodies, receive their reward, and dwell forever with the Lord
Believers will be judged again and may lose their salvation
Believers will become angels and serve in God's heavenly court

questions.question: What does the Bible tell us about Heaven?
questions.answer: It is the place from which God reigns over the universe. It is a perfect place without sin or suffering.

It is the place from which God reigns over the universe. It is a perfect place without sin or suffering
It is a place free from suffering where people still struggle against sin
It is a spiritual realm beyond time and space, not a literal place

questions.question: What is the responsibility of every Christian?

To keep the law of Moses so as to earn God's favor
To leave witnessing to pastors and missionaries while serving at home
To withdraw from the world so as to keep free from its sin

questions.answer: Missions is evangelism that reaches people from another culture or who speak another language. It is not enough to reach people like us in our own community. The Lord Jesus Christ has commanded the preaching of the gospel to all nations.

Evangelism limited to people like us in our own community
Giving relief to the poor in other lands without sharing the gospel
Evangelism to people of other cultures and languages; preaching the gospel to all nations

questions.question: What is Christian stewardship?
questions.answer: Stewardship is managing something that belongs to someone else, using it the way its owner wants it used. Everything we have comes from God and belongs to Him. Christians are stewards of their time, talents, and material possessions. Most importantly, we are stewards of the Gospel.
options: Owning your time and possessions and using them as you see fit
Saving money carefully so that you and your family are never in need
Managing God's resources—time, talents, possessions, Gospel—the way God wants
Holding offices in the church and serving on its committees

questions.question: How should the Christian give to the Lord's work?
questions.answer: Christians should give to the Lord's work cheerfully, regularly, and generously. The more they make the more they should give.

Christians should give to the Lord's work only what is left over after their own wants are met
Christians should sacrifice and give sacrificially until they have less than others
Christians should give to the Lord's work cheerfully, regularly, and generously. The more they make the more they should give

God's creation; two people united in love and commitment for life together

questions.question: Are Baptists the only true church?

audit.why: The three wrong choices were all true statements about Christ's blood, so they could be picked fairly; they are replaced with clearly wrong but believable reasons, and the right answer is unchanged. Rechecked against the verses that hold the answer: The answer is right but its reference only cited 1 Peter 1:19, which shows Christ was "without blemish or spot" yet does not by itself state He was born without sin and never sinned; Hebrews 7:26 and 1 John 3:5 supply that, so the reference now lists all three verses.

grounding.note: Christ's blood is holy because He is sinless: 1 Peter 1:19 calls Him a lamb without blemish, Hebrews 7:26 says He is holy, innocent, and undefiled, and 1 John 3:5 says there is no sin in Him.
grounding.doubt: The verses show that Christ was holy and never sinned, but none of them says He was born without sin, so that part of the answer goes beyond them.

options: By His human nature alone He could endure God's wrath and obtain righteousness for us
By His teachings He showed humanity how to bear God's wrath and gain eternal life
By His divine power He can bear God's wrath, obtaining and restoring for us righteousness and life
By His divine mercy He forgave all sins and granted righteousness without bearing wrath

questions.question: According to the Heidelberg Catechism, what is true faith?
questions.answer: True faith is a sure knowledge whereby I accept as true all that God has revealed to us in His Word. At the same time it is a firm confidence that not only to others, but also to me, God has granted forgiveness of sins, everlasting righteousness, and salvation, out of mere grace, only for the sake of Christ's merits. This faith the Holy Spirit works in my heart by the gospel.
options: A feeling, produced by my own will, that God is pleased with me
Sure knowledge of God's Word and firm confidence that Christ's merits save me by grace
Knowing that God exists, even as the demons believe, without personal trust in Him
A hope that God will forgive me if my good works outweigh my sins

questions.question: What do you believe when you say: I believe in God the Father almighty, Creator of heaven and earth?

In Him I trust so completely as to have no doubt that He will provide me with all things necessary for body and soul, and will also turn to my good whatever adversity He sends me in this life of sorrow. questions.answer: Christ speaks in this way for a good reason: He wants to teach us by His supper that as bread and wine sustain us in this temporal life, so His crucified body and shed blood are true food and drink for our souls to eternal life. But, even more important, He wants to assure us by this visible sign and pledge, first, that through the working of the Holy Spirit we share in His true body and blood as surely as we receive with our mouth these holy signs in remembrance of Him, and, second, that all His suffering and obedience are as certainly ours as if we personally had suffered and paid for our sins.
options: The bread and wine are merely symbols of Christ's body and blood with no real spiritual significance to believers
The bread and wine physically transform into His body and blood through the priest's consecration for literal consumption
Through priestly blessing, Christ's body is daily re-offered for the sins of both living and dead
Bread nourishes bodies as His body nourishes souls eternally; by Spirit we truly share in Him and His suffering becomes ours.

questions.question: What difference is there between the Lord's supper and the papal mass?
questions.answer: The Lord's supper testifies to us, first, that we have complete forgiveness of all our sins through the one sacrifice of Jesus Christ, which He Himself accomplished on the cross once for all; and, second, that through the Holy Spirit we are grafted into Christ, who with His true body is now in heaven at the right hand of the Father, and this is where He wants to be worshipped. But the mass teaches, first, that the living and the dead do not have forgiveness of sins through the suffering of Christ unless He is still offered for them daily by the priests; and, second, that Christ is bodily present in the form of bread and wine, and there is to be worshipped. Therefore the mass is basically nothing but a denial of the one sacrifice and suffering of Jesus Christ, and an accursed idolatry.
options: Both Supper and mass teach that Christ is present in the bread and wine to be worshipped by believers
The Lord's Supper teaches that forgiveness needs daily offering by priests, while the mass rests on Christ's one sacrifice on the cross
Supper witnesses complete forgiveness through Christ's one sacrifice; mass wrongly teaches daily re-offering and worship of Christ bodily present in bread.
The Lord's Supper and the mass are essentially the same, both offering Christ's sacrifice daily for the living and dead

questions.question: What does the LORD require in the first commandment?
questions.answer: That for the sake of my very salvation I avoid and flee all idolatry, witchcraft, superstition, and prayer to saints or to other creatures. Further, that I rightly come to know the only true God, trust in Him alone, submit to Him with all humility and patience, expect all good from Him only, and love, fear, and honor Him with all my heart. In short, that I forsake all creatures rather than do the least thing against His will.

questions.question: How is justification an act of God's free grace?
questions.answer: Although Christ, by his obedience and death, did make a proper, real, and full satisfaction to God's justice in the behalf of them that are justified; yet inasmuch as God accepteth the satisfaction from a surety, which he might have demanded of them, and did provide this surety, his own only Son, imputing his righteousness to them, and requiring nothing of them for their justification but faith, which also is his gift, their justification is to them of free grace.

Christ made full satisfaction through the law; God accepts human effort from believers and imputes faith as righteousness.
Christ made partial satisfaction for the justified; God accepts works with faith and imputes sanctification for justification.

questions.question: What is justifying faith?

questions.answer: Faith justifies a sinner in the sight of God, not because of the other graces that always accompany it, or because of good works that are its fruits, nor because the grace of faith or any act of it is credited to him for his justification; but only because it is the instrument by which he receives and applies Christ and His righteousness.

questions.question: Wherein do justification and sanctification differ?
questions.answer: Although sanctification be inseparably joined with justification, yet they differ, in that God in justification imputeth the righteousness of Christ; in sanctification his Spirit infuseth grace, and enableth to the exercise thereof; in the former, sin is pardoned; in the other, it is subdued: the one doth equally free all believers from the revenging wrath of God, and that perfectly in this life, that they never fall into condemnation; the other is neither equal in all, nor in this life perfect in any, but growing up to perfection.

Justification pardons sin gradually through faith; sanctification immediately frees from wrath and infuses perfect holiness eternally.

questions.question: What rules are to be observed for the right understanding of the ten commandments?
questions.answer: For the right understanding of the ten commandments, these rules are to be observed: 1. That the law is perfect, and binds everyone to full conformity in the whole man to its righteousness, and to entire obedience forever; so as to require the utmost perfection of every duty, and to forbid the least degree of every sin. 2. That it is spiritual, and so reaches the understanding, will, affections, and all other powers of the soul, as well as words, works, and gestures. 3. That one and the same thing, in different respects, is required or forbidden in several commandments. 4. That as, where a duty is commanded, the contrary sin is forbidden; and where a sin is forbidden, the contrary duty is commanded: so, where a promise is given, the contrary warning is included; and where a warning is given, the contrary promise is included. 5. That what God forbids is never to be done; what He commands is always our duty; yet not every particular duty is to be done at all times. 6. That under one sin or duty, all of the same kind are forbidden or commanded, together with all the causes, means, occasions, and appearances of it, and temptations to it. 7. That what is forbidden or commanded to ourselves, we are bound, according to our places, to try to see it avoided or performed by others, according to the duty of their places. 8. That in what is commanded to others, we are bound, according to our places and callings, to help them; and to take care not to share with others in what is forbidden them.
options: The law is a perfect guide requiring external conformity; it is rational and reaches the mind and will.
The law is absolutely binding to external obedience, concerning actions and words; it forbids gross transgressions only.
The law is perfect binding to reasonable effort, spiritual reaching the heart only, with each duty confined to one commandment
The law is perfect binding to complete conformity, spiritual reaching all powers, with duties commanded and sins forbidden in commandments

questions.question: How is the sabbath or the Lord's day to be sanctified?
questions.answer: The sabbath or Lord's day is to be sanctified by an holy resting all the day, not only from such works as are at all times sinful, but even from such worldly employments and recreations as are on other days lawful; and making it our delight to spend the whole time (except so much of it as is to betaken up in works of necessity and mercy) in the public and private exercises of God's worship: and, to that end, we are to prepare our hearts, and with such foresight, diligence, and moderation, to dispose and seasonably dispatch our worldly business, that we may be the more free and fit for the duties of that day.

questions.answer: The word Remember is set in the beginning of the fourth commandment, partly, because of the great benefit of remembering it, we being thereby helped in our preparation to keep it, and, in keeping it, better to keep all the rest of the commandments, and to continue a thankful remembrance of the two great benefits of creation and redemption, which contain a short abridgment of religion; and partly, because we are very ready to forget it, for that there is less light of nature for it, and yet it restraineth our natural liberty in things at other times lawful; that it comes but once in seven days, and many worldly businesses come between, and too often take off our minds from thinking of it, either to prepare for it, or to sanctify it; and that Satan with his instruments much labor to blot out the glory, and even the memory of it, to bring in all irreligion and impiety.
options: The word Remember is included to remind us that the Sabbath was created for human convenience and leisure
The word Remember shows that the Sabbath was a new law, first given at Sinai
Remembering helps us keep it and all the commandments, and we are very ready to forget it
Remembering the Sabbath means taking time for rest alone, without concern for spiritual worship or creation's significance

Named Father and Mother because superiors must exercise firm discipline and correction over inferiors, like fathers discipline children

questions.answer: Sins receive their aggravations, 1. From the persons offending: if they be of riper age, greater experience or grace, eminent for profession, gifts, place, office, guides to others, and whose example is likely to be followed by others. 2. From the parties offended: if immediately against God, his attributes, and worship; against Christ, and his grace; the Holy Spirit, his witness, and workings; against superiors, men of eminency, and such as we stand especially related and engaged unto; against any of the saints, particularly weak brethren, the souls of them, or any other, and the common good of all or many. 3. From the nature and quality of the offense: if it be against the express letter of the law, break many commandments, contain in it many sins: if not only conceived in the heart, but breaks forth in words and actions, scandalize others, and admit of no reparation: if against means, mercies, judgments, light of nature, conviction of conscience, public or private admonition, censures of the church, civil punishments; and our prayers, purposes, promises, vows, covenants, and engagements to God or men: if done deliberately, wilfully, presumptuously, impudently, boastingly, maliciously, frequently, obstinately, with delight, continuance, or relapsing after repentance. 4. From circumstances of time and place: if on the Lord's day, or other times of divine worship; or immediately before or after these, or other helps to prevent or remedy such miscarriages: if in public, or in the presence of others, who are thereby likely to be provoked or defiled.
options: From the sinner's knowledge, position, and power; offense against superiors; and public commission
From breaking express law, offense against the innocent, violation of sacred time, and malice
From the sinner's deliberate intent and resistance to correction, scandal caused, and persistence
From the persons offending, parties offended, nature of offense, and circumstances of time and place

questions.question: What do we pray for in the first petition?
questions.answer: In the first petition (which is, Hallowed be thy name,) acknowledging the utter inability and indisposition that is in ourselves and all men to honor God aright, pray, that God would by his grace enable and incline us and others to know, to acknowledge, and highly to esteem him, his titles, attributes, ordinances, word, works, and whatsoever he is pleased to make himself known by; and to glorify him in thought, word, and deed: that he would prevent and remove atheism, ignorance, idolatry, profaneness, and: whatsoever is dishonorable to him; and, by his overruling providence, direct and dispose of all things to his own glory.

questions.question: What do we pray for in the second petition.?
questions.answer: In the second petition (which is, Thy kingdom come,) acknowledging ourselves and all mankind to be by nature under the dominion of sin and Satan, we pray, that the kingdom of sin and Satan may be destroyed, the gospel propagated throughout the world, the Jews called, the fulness of the Gentiles brought in; the church furnished with all gospel officers and ordinances, purged from corruption, countenanced and maintained by the civil magistrate: that the ordinances of Christ may be purely dispensed, and made effectual to the converting of those that are yet in their sins, and the confirming, comforting, and building up of those that are already converted: that Christ would rule in our hearts here, and hasten the time of his second coming, and our reigning with him forever: and that he would be pleased so to exercise the kingdom of his power in all the world, as may best conduce to these ends.

questions.question: What do we pray for in the third petition?
questions.answer: In the third petition (which is, Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven,) acknowledging, that by nature we and all men are not only utterly unable and unwilling to know and do the will of God, but prone to rebel against his word, to repine and murmur against his providence, and wholly inclined to do the will of the flesh, and of the devil: we pray, that God would by his Spirit take away from ourselves and others all blindness, weakness, indisposedness, and perverseness of heart; and by his grace make us able and willing to know, do, and submit to his will in all things, with the like humility, cheerfulness, faithfulness, diligence, zeal, sincerity, and constancy, as the angels do in heaven.

questions.question: What do we pray for in the fourth petition?
questions.answer: In the fourth petition (which is, Give us this day our daily bread,) acknowledging, that in Adam, and by our own sin, we have forfeited our right to all the outward blessings of this life, and deserve to be wholly deprived of them by God, and to have them cursed to us in the use of them; and that neither they of themselves are able to sustain us, nor we to merit, or by our own industry to procure them; but prone to desire, get, and use them unlawfully: we pray for ourselves and others, that both they and we, waiting upon the providence of God from day to day in the use of lawful means, may, of his free gift, and as to his fatherly wisdom shall seem best, enjoy a competent portion of them; and have the same continued and blessed unto us in our holy and comfortable use of them, and contentment in them; and be kept from all things that are contrary to our temporal support and comfort.

questions.question: What do we pray for in the fifth petition?
questions.answer: In the fifth petition (which is, Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors,) acknowledging, that we and all others are guilty both of original and actual sin, and thereby become debtors to the justice of God; and that neither we, nor any other creature, can make the least satisfaction for that debt: we pray for ourselves and others, that God of his free grace would, through the obedience and satisfaction of Christ, apprehended and applied by faith, acquit us both from the guilt and punishment of sin, accept us in his Beloved; continue his favor and grace to us, pardon our daily failings, and fill us with peace and joy, in giving us daily more and more assurance of forgiveness; which we are the rather emboldened to ask, and encouraged to expect, when we have this testimony in ourselves, that we from the heart forgive others their offenses.

questions.question: What do we pray for in the sixth petition?
questions.answer: In the sixth petition (which is, And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil,) acknowledging, that the most wise, righteous, and gracious God, for divers holy and just ends, may so order things, that we may be assaulted, foiled, and for a time led captive by temptations; that Satan, the world, and the flesh, are ready powerfully to draw us aside, and ensnare us; and that we, even after the pardon of our sins, by reason of our corruption, weakness, and want of watchfulness, are not only subject to be tempted, and forward to expose ourselves unto temptations, but also of ourselves unable and unwilling to resist them, to recover out of them, and to improve them; and worthy to be left under the power of them: we pray, that God would so overrule the world and all in it, subdue the flesh, and restrain Satan, order all things, bestow and bless all means of grace, and quicken us to watchfulness in the use of them, that we and all his people may by his providence be kept from being tempted to sin; or, if tempted, that by his Spirit we may be powerfully supported and enabled to stand in the hour of temptation; or when fallen, raised again and recovered out of it, and have a sanctified use and improvement thereof: that our sanctification and salvation may be perfected, Satan trodden under our feet, and we fully freed from sin, temptation, and all evil, forever.

questions.question: What doth the conclusion of the Lord's prayer teach us?
questions.answer: The conclusion of the Lord's prayer (which is, For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever. questions.question: Wherein consisteth the sinfulness of that estate whereinto man fell?
questions.answer: The sinfulness of that estate whereinto man fell, consisteth in the guilt of Adam's first sin, the want of that righteousness wherein he was created, and the corruption of his nature, whereby he is utterly indisposed, disabled, and made opposite unto all that is spiritually good, and wholly inclined to all evil, and that continually; which is commonly called original sin, and from which do proceed all actual transgressions.

questions.question: What are the punishments of sin in this world?
questions.answer: The punishments of sin in this world are either inward, as blindness of mind, a reprobate sense, strong delusions, hardness of heart, horror of conscience, and vile affections; or outward, as the curse of God upon the creatures of our sakes, and all other evils that befall us in our bodies, names, estates, relations, and employments; together with death itself.

questions.question: How was the covenant of grace administered under the Old Testament?
questions.answer: The covenant of grace was administered under the Old Testament, by promises, prophecies, sacrifices, circumcision, the passover, and other types and ordinances, which did all fore-signify Christ then to come, and were for that time sufficient to build up the elect in faith in the promised Messiah, by whom they then had full remission of sin, and eternal salvation.

questions.question: Why was it requisite that the Mediator should be God?
questions.answer: It was requisite that the Mediator should be God, that he might sustain and keep the human nature from sinking under the infinite wrath of God, and the power of death, give worth and efficacy to his sufferings, obedience, and intercession; and to satisfy God's justice, procure his favour, purchase a peculiar people, give his Spirit to them, conquer all their enemies, and bring them to everlasting salvation.

questions.question: How doth Christ execute the office of a priest?
questions.answer: Christ executeth the office of a priest, in his once offering himself a sacrifice without spot to God, to be reconciliation for the sins of his people; and in making continual intercession for them.

questions.question: How was Christ exalted in his ascension?
questions.answer: Christ was exalted in his ascension, in that having after his resurrection often appeared unto and conversed with his apostles, speaking to them of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God, and giving them commission to preach the gospel to all nations, forty days after his resurrection, he, in our nature, and as our head, triumphing over enemies, visibly went up into the highest heavens, there to receive gifts for men, to raise up our affections thither, and to prepare a place for us, where he himself is, and shall continue till his second coming at the end of the world.

questions.question: How is Christ exalted in his sitting at the right hand of God?
questions.answer: Christ is exalted in his sitting at the right hand of God, in that as God-man he is advanced to the highest favour with God the Father, with all fulness of joy, glory, and power over all things in heaven and earth; and does gather and defend his church, and subdue their enemies; furnisheth his ministers and people with gifts and graces, and maketh intercession for them.

questions.question: How doeth Christ make intercession?
questions.answer: Christ maketh intercession, by his appearing in our nature continually before the Father in heaven, in the merit of his obedience and sacrifice on earth, declaring his will to have it applied to all believers; answering all accusations against them, and procuring for them quiet of conscience, notwithstanding daily failings, access with boldness to the throne of grace, and acceptance of their persons and services.

questions.question: What are the special privileges of the visible church?
questions.answer: The visible church hath the privilege of being under God’s special care and government; of being protected and preserved in all ages, notwithstanding the opposition of all enemies; and of enjoying the communion of saints, the ordinary means of salvation, and offers of grace by Christ to all the members of it in the ministry of the gospel, testifying, that whosoever believes in him shall be saved, and excluding none that will come unto him.

questions.question: How is justification an act of God’s free grace?
questions.answer: Although Christ, by his obedience and death, did make a proper, real, and full satisfaction to God’s justice in the behalf of them that are justified; yet in as much as God accepteth the satisfaction from a surety, which he might have demanded of them, and did provide this surety, his own only Son, imputing his righteousness to them, and requiring nothing of them for their justification but faith, which also is his gift, their justification is to them of free grace.

questions.question: How doth faith justify a sinner in the sight of God?
questions.answer: Faith justifies a sinner in the sight of God, not because of those other graces which do always accompany it, or of good works that are the fruits of it, nor as if the grace of faith, or any act thereof, were imputed to him for his justification; but only as it is an instrument by which he receiveth and applieth Christ and his righteousness.

questions.question: What is repentance unto life?
questions.answer: Repentance unto life is a saving grace, wrought in the heart of a sinner by the Spirit and Word of God, whereby, out of the sight and sense, not only of the danger, but also of the filthiness and odiousness of his sins, and upon the apprehension of God’s mercy in Christ to such as are penitent, he so grieves for and hates his sins, as that he turns from them all to God, purposing and endeavouring constantly to walk with him in all the ways of new obedience.

questions.question: Wherein do justification and sanctification differ?
questions.answer: Although sanctification be inseparably joined with justification, yet they differ, in that God in justification imputeth the righteousness of Christ; in sanctification of his Spirit infuseth grace, and enableth to the exercise thereof; in the former, sin is pardoned; in the other, it is subdued: the one doth equally free all believers from the revenging wrath of God, and that perfectly in this life, that they never fall into condemnation the other is neither equal in all, nor in this life perfect in any, but growing up to perfection.

questions.question: Can true believers be infallibly assured that they are in the estate of grace, and that they shall persevere therein unto salvation?
questions.answer: Such as truly believe in Christ, and endeavour to walk in all good conscience before him, may, without extraordinary revelation, by faith grounded upon the truth of God’s promises, and by the Spirit enabling them to discern in themselves those graces to which the promises of life are made, and bearing witness with their spirits that they are the children of God, be infallibly assured that they are in the estate of grace, and shall persevere therein unto salvation.

questions.question: Are all true believers at all times assured of their present being in the estate of grace, and that they shall be saved?
questions.answer: Assurance of grace and salvation not being of the essence of faith, true believers may wait long before they obtain it; and, after the enjoyment thereof, may have it weakened and intermitted, through manifold distempers, sins, temptations, and desertions; yet they are never left without such a presence and support of the Spirit of God as keeps them from sinking into utter despair.

questions.question: What are we to believe concerning the resurrection?
questions.answer: We are to believe that at the last day there shall be a general resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust: when they that are then found alive shall in a moment be changed; and the selfsame bodies of the dead which were laid in the grave, being then again united to their souls forever, shall be raised up by the power of Christ. The bodies of the just, by the Spirit of Christ, and by virtue of his resurrection as their head, shall be raised in power, spiritual, incorruptible, and made like to his glorious body; and the bodies of the wicked shall be raised up in dishonour by him, as an offended judge.

questions.question: What shall immediately follow after the resurrection?
questions.answer: Immediately after the resurrection shall follow the general and final judgment of angels and men; the day and hour whereof no man knoweth, that all may watch and pray, and be ever ready for the coming of the Lord.

questions.question: What shall be done to the wicked at the day of judgment?
questions.answer: At the day of judgment, the wicked shall be set on Christ’s left hand, and, upon clear evidence, and full conviction of their own consciences, shall have the fearful but just sentence of condemnation pronounced against them; and thereupon shall be cast out from the favourable presence of God, and the glorious fellowship with Christ, his saints, and all his holy angels, into hell, to be punished with unspeakable torments, both of body and soul, with the devil and his angels forever.

questions.question: What did God at first reveal unto man as the rule of his obedience?
questions.answer: The rule of obedience revealed to Adam in the estate of innocence, and to all mankind in him, besides a special command not to eat of the fruit of the tree knowledge of good and evil, was the moral law.

questions.question: What is the moral law?
questions.answer: The moral law is the declaration of the will of God to mankind, directing and binding every one to personal, perfect, and perpetual conformity and obedience thereunto, in the frame and disposition of the whole man, soul and body, and in performance of all those duties of holiness and righteousness which he oweth to God and man: promising life upon the fulfilling, and threatening death upon the breach of it.

questions.question: Of what use is the moral law to all men?
questions.answer: The moral law is of use to all men, to inform them of the holy nature and the will of God, and of their duty, binding them to walk accordingly; to convince them of their disability to keep it, and of the sinful pollution of their nature, hearts, and lives: to humble them in the sense of their sin and misery, and thereby help them to a clearer sight of the need they have of Christ, and of the perfection of his obedience.

questions.question: What rules are to be observed for the right understanding of the ten commandments?
questions.answer: For the right understanding of the ten commandments, these rules are to be observed: 1. That the law is perfect, and bindeth everyone to full conformity in the whole man unto the righteousness thereof, and unto entire obedience forever; so as to require the utmost perfection of every duty, and to forbid the least degree of every sin. 2. That it is spiritual, and so reacheth the understanding, will, affections, and all other powers of the soul; as well as words, works, and gestures. 3. That one and the same thing, in divers respects, is required or forbidden in several commandments. 4. That as, where a duty is commanded, the contrary sin is forbidden; and, where a sin is forbidden, the contrary duty is commanded: so, where a promise is annexed, the contrary threatening is included; and, where a threatening is annexed, the contrary promise is included. 5. That what God forbids, is at no time to be done; what he commands, is always our duty; and yet every particular duty is not to be done at all times. 6. That under one sin or duty, all of the same kind are forbidden or commanded; together with all the causes, means, occasions, and appearances thereof, and provocations thereunto. 7. That what is forbidden or commanded to ourselves, we are bound, according to our places to endeavour that it may be avoided or performed by others, according to the duty of their places. 8. That in what is commanded to others, we are bound, according to our places and callings, to be helpful to them; and to take heed of partaking with others in what is forbidden them.

questions.question: What is the preface to the ten commandments?
questions.answer: The preface to the ten commandments is contained in these words, I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Wherein God manifesteth his sovereignty, as being JEHOVAH, the eternal, immutable, and almighty God; having his being in and of himself, and giving being to all his words and works: and that he is a God in covenant, as with Israel of old, so with all his people; who, as he brought them out of their bondage in Egypt, so he delivereth us from our spiritual thraldom; and that therefore we are bound to take him for our God alone, and to keep all his commandments.

questions.question: What are the duties required in the first commandment?
questions.answer: The duties required in the first commandment are, the knowing and acknowledging of God to be the only true God, and our God; and to worship and glorify him accordingly, by thinking, meditating, remembering, highly esteeming, honouring, adoring, choosing, loving, desiring, fearing of him; believing him; trusting hoping, delighting, rejoicing in him; being zealous for him; calling upon him, giving all praise and thanks, and yielding all obedience and submission to him with the whole man; being careful in all things to please him, and sorrowful when in any thing he is offended; and walking humbly with him.

questions.question: What are the sins forbidden in the first commandment?
questions.answer: The sins forbidden in the first commandment are, atheism, in denying or not having a God; idolatry, in having or worshipping more gods than one, or any with or instead of the true God; the not having and avouching him for God, and our God; the omission or neglect of anything due to him, required in this commandment; ignorance, forgetfulness, misapprehensions, false opinions, unworthy and wicked thoughts of him; bold and curious searching into his secrets; all profaneness, hatred of God; self-love, self-seeking, and all other inordinate and immoderate setting of our mind, will, or affections upon other things, and taking them off from him in whole or in part; vain credulity, unbelief, heresy, misbelief, distrust, despair, incorrigibleness, and insensibleness under judgments, hardness of heart, pride, presumption, carnal security, tempting of God; using unlawful means, and trusting in lawful means; carnal delights and joys; corrupt, blind, and indiscreet zeal; lukewarmness, and deadness in the things of God; estranging ourselves, and apostatizing from God; praying, or giving any religious worship, to saints, angels, or any other creatures; all compacts and consulting with the devil, and hearkening to his suggestions; making men the lords of our faith and conscience; slighting and despising God and his commands; resisting and grieving of his Spirit, discontent and impatience at his dispensations, charging him foolishly for the evils he inflicts on us; and ascribing the praise of any good we either are, have or can do, to fortune, idols, ourselves, or any other creature.

questions.question: Which is the second commandment?
questions.answer: The second commandment is, Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth. Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and showing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.

questions.question: What are the duties required in the second commandment?
questions.answer: The duties required in the second commandment are, the receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire, all such religious worship and ordinances as God hath instituted in his Word; particularly prayer and thanksgiving in the name of Christ; the reading, preaching, and hearing of the Word; the administration and receiving of the sacraments; church government and discipline; the ministry and maintainance thereof; religious fasting; swearing by the name of God; and vowing unto him; as also the disapproving, detesting, opposing all false worship; and, according to each one’s place and calling, removing it, and all monuments of idolatry.

questions.question: What are the sins forbidden in the second commandment?
questions.answer: The sins forbidden in the second commandment are, all devising, counselling, commanding, using, and anywise approving, any religious worship not instituted by God himself; tolerating a false religion; the making any representation of God, of all or of any of the three persons, either inwardly in our mind, or outwardly in any kind of image or likeness of any creature whatsoever; all worshipping of it, or God in it or by it; the making of any representation of feigned deities, and all worship of them, or service belonging to them, all superstitious devices, corrupting the worship of God, adding to it, or taking from it, whether invented and taken up of ourselves, or received by tradition from others, though under the title of antiquity, custom, devotion, good intent, or any other pretence whatsoever; simony; sacrilege; all neglect, contempt, hindering, and opposing the worship and ordinances which God hath appointed..

questions.question: What are the sins forbidden in the third commandment?
questions.answer: The sins forbidden in the third commandment are, the not using of God’s name as is required; and the abuse of it in an ignorant, vain, irreverent, profane, superstitious or wicked mentioning or otherwise using his titles, attributes, ordinances, or works, by blasphemy, perjury; all sinful cursings, oaths, vows, and lots; violating of our oaths and vows, if lawful and fulfilling them, if of things unlawful; murmuring and quarrelling at, curious prying into, and misapplying of God’s decrees and providences; misinterpreting, misapplying, or any way perverting the Word, or any part of it; to profane jests, curious or unprofitable questions, vain janglings, or the maintaining of false doctrines; abusing it, the creatures, or anything contained under the name of God, to charms, or sinful lusts and practices; the maligning, scorning, reviling, or any wise opposing of God’s truth, grace, and ways; making profession of religion in hypocrisy, or for sinister ends; being ashamed of it, or a shame to it, by unconformable, unwise, unfruitful, and offensive walking, or backsliding from it..

questions.question: Which is the fourth commandment?
questions.answer: The fourth commandment is, Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work; but the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy man-servant, nor thy maid-servant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates. For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested in the seventh day: wherefore the Lord blessed the sabbath-day and hallowed it..

questions.question: What is required in the fourth commandment?
questions.answer: The fourth commandment requireth of all men the sanctifying or keeping holy to God such set times as he hath appointed in his Word, expressly one whole day in seven; which was the seventh from the beginning of the world to the resurrection of Christ, and the first day of the week ever since, and so to continue to the end of the world; which is the Christian sabbath, and in the New Testament called The Lord’s day.

questions.question: How is the sabbath or the Lord’s day to be sanctified?
questions.answer: The sabbath or Lord’s day is to be sanctified by an holy resting all the day, not only from such works as are at all times sinful, but even from such worldly employments and recreations as are on other days lawful; and making it our delight to spend the whole time (except so much of it as is to be taken up in works of necessity and mercy) in the public and private exercises of God’s worship: and, to that end, we are to prepare our hearts, and with such foresight, diligence, and moderation, to dispose and seasonably dispatch our worldly business, that we may be the more free and fit for the duties of that day.

questions.question: What are the reasons annexed to the fourth commandment, the more to enforce it?
questions.answer: The reasons annexed to the fourth commandment, the more to enforce it, are taken from the equity of it, God allowing us six days of seven for our own affairs, and reserving but one for himself in these words, Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: from God’s challenging a special propriety in that day, The seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: from the example of God, who in six days made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: and from that blessing which God put upon that day, not only in sanctifying it to be a day for his service, but in ordaining it to be a means of blessing to us in our sanctifying it; Wherefore the Lord blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.

questions.question: Why is the word Remember set in the beginning of the fourth commandment?
questions.answer: The word Remember is set in the beginning of the fourth commandment, partly, because of the great benefit of remembering it, we being thereby helped in our preparation to keep it, and, in keeping it, better to keep all the rest of the commandments, and to continue a thankful remembrance of the two great benefits of creation and redemption, which contain a short abridgment of religion; and partly, because we are very ready to forget it, for that there is less light of nature for it, and yet it restraineth our natural liberty in things at other times lawful; that it cometh but once in seven days, and many worldly businesses come between, and too often take off our minds from thinking of it, either to prepare for it, or to sanctify it; and that Satan with his instruments labours much to blot out the glory, and even the memory of it, to bring in all irreligion and impiety.

questions.question: What is the sum of the six commandments which contain our duty to man?
questions.answer: The sum of the six commandments which contain our duty to man, is, to love our neighbour as ourselves, and to do to others what we would have them to do to us.

questions.question: What is the honour that inferiors owe to their superiors?
questions.answer: The honour which inferiors owe to their superiors is, all due reverence in heart, word, and behaviour; prayer and thanksgiving for them; imitation of their virtues and graces; willing obedience to their lawful commands and counsels; due submission to their corrections; fidelity to, defence, and maintenance of their persons and authority, according to their several ranks, and the nature of their places; bearing with their infirmities, and covering them in love, that so they may be an honour to them and to their government.

questions.question: What are the sins of inferiors against their superiors?
questions.answer: The sins of inferiors against their superiors are, all neglect of the duties required toward them; envying at, contempt of, and rebellion against, their persons and places, in their lawful counsels, commands, and corrections; cursing, mocking and all such refractory and scandalous carriage, as proves a shame and dishonour to them and their government.

questions.question: What is required of superiors towards their inferiors?
questions.answer: It is required of superiors, according to that power they receive from God, and that relation wherein they stand, to love, pray for, and bless their inferiors; to instruct, counsel, and admonish them; countenancing, commending, and rewarding such as do well; and discountenancing, reproving, and chastising such as do ill; protecting, and providing for them all things necessary for soul and body: and by grave, wise, holy, and exemplary carriage, to procure glory to God, honour to themselves, and so to preserve that authority which God hath put upon them.

questions.question: What are the sins of superiors?
questions.answer: The sins of superiors are, besides the neglect of the duties required of them, and inordinate seeking of themselves, their own glory, ease, profit, or pleasure; commanding things unlawful, or not in the power of inferiors to perform; counseling, encouraging, or favouring them in that which is evil; dissuading, discouraging, or discountenancing them in that which is good; correcting them unduly; careless exposing, or leaving them to wrong, temptation, and danger; provoking them to wrath; or any way dishonouring themselves, or lessening their authority, by an unjust, indiscreet, rigorous, or remiss behaviour.

questions.question: What are the duties of equals?
questions.answer: The duties of equals are, to regard the dignity and worth of each other, in giving honour to go one before another; and to rejoice in each others’ gifts and advancement, as their own.

questions.question: What are the sins of equals?
questions.answer: The sins of equals are, besides the neglect of the duties required, the undervaluing of the worth, envying the gifts, grieving at the advancement of prosperity one of another; and usurping pre-eminence one over another.

questions.question: What are the duties required in the sixth commandment?
questions.answer: The duties required in the sixth commandment are all careful studies, and lawful endeavors, to preserve the life of ourselves and others by resisting all thoughts and purposes, subduing all passions, and avoiding all occasions, temptations, and practices, which tend to the unjust taking away the life of any; by just defence thereof against violence, patient bearing of the hand of God, quietness of mind, cheerfulness of spirit; a sober use of meat, drink, physic, sleep, labour, and recreations; by charitable thoughts, love, compassion, meekness, gentleness, kindness; peaceable, mild and courteous speeches and behaviour; forbearance, readiness to be reconciled, patient bearing and forgiving of injuries, and requiting good for evil; comforting and succouring the distressed and protecting and defending the innocent.
